Note::NlpAccessor::normalize_punct¶

Back to Note NLP Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::NlpAccessor::normalize_punct(bool ascii_only = false) const

Canonicalize Common Typographic Punctuation¶

normalize_punct() reduces visually equivalent punctuation to stable byte sequences before matching, tokenization, hashing, or equality checks. It combines three focused transformations in one public operation:

Input family

Recognized characters

Output

Single quotes

‘ ’ ‚ ‛

'

Double quotes

“ ” „ ‟

"

Dashes

hyphen, non-breaking hyphen, figure dash, en dash, em dash, horizontal bar, minus sign

-

Ellipsis

…

...

ASCII punctuation already in canonical form is unchanged. The method does not collapse repeated ASCII punctuation, remove punctuation, normalize whitespace, or infer paired quotation structure.

The overloads differ only in their treatment of all remaining non-ASCII characters:

Call form

ascii_only

Remaining non-ASCII text

normalize_punct()

false

Preserved as UTF-8.

normalize_punct(false)

false

Identical to the no-argument form.

normalize_punct(true)

true

Each UTF-8 code point becomes one ?.

The true mode is intentionally lossy ASCII enforcement, not transliteration. For example, the single code point ï becomes one question mark rather than i. Typographic quotes and dashes are converted before that enforcement, so they retain their meaningful ASCII equivalents instead of becoming ?.

Each cell is independent, and both overloads allocate a new shape-identical Text Note without mutating the receiver. The operation is idempotent in either mode. Empty Text Notes remain empty, undefined propagates, and Bytes, Bool, Int64, and Float64 Notes reject.

Example 1: Preserve Non-ASCII Vocabulary By Default¶

const auto punct = pluss::note::make({"“naïve”—wait…"});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    punct.nlp().normalize_punct()) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["\"naïve\"-wait..."]

Example 2: Spell Out The Default Explicitly¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    punct.nlp().normalize_punct(false)) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["\"naïve\"-wait..."]

Example 3: Request Lossy ASCII Output¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    punct.nlp().normalize_punct(true)) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["\"na?ve\"-wait..."]

Example 4: Punctuation Normalization Does Not Clean Other Content¶

const auto matrix = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<std::string>{" can't ", "12", "“yes”", "plain"},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    matrix.nlp().normalize_punct()) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  [" can't ", "12"], 
  ["\"yes\"", "plain"]
]

The spaces, contraction, digits, and case remain because this method changes only its documented punctuation families.

See Also¶

  • normalize_quotes: normalize only quote characters.

  • normalize_dashes: normalize only dash characters.

  • normalize_ellipsis: normalize only the ellipsis code point.
